title: Continuous uniform delivery window: density height and interval area
scenario_markdown: A local courier service guarantees package delivery uniformly distributed between 10 and 40 minutes after an order is dispatched ($X \sim U(10, 40)$). Determine the probability density height and calculate the probability that a customer receives their delivery between 15 and 25 minutes.
assumptions: Constant probability density f(x) = 1/(b - a) on support [10, 40]

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the constant probability density height $f(x)$ for deliveries between 10 and 40 minutes?

options.hint_markdown: Total area under the PDF must equal 1, so the height is the reciprocal of the width: $1/(b-a)$.
25 is the mean delivery time $(a+b)/2$, not the density height.

stages.explanation_markdown: For a continuous uniform distribution $U(a, b)$, the total area under $f(x)$ must equal 1: $\text{Area} = \text{width} \times \text{height} = (b - a) \times f(x) = 1 \implies f(x) = \frac{1}{b - a} = \frac{1}{40 - 10} = \frac{1}{30} \approx 0.0333$ per minute.

stages.prompt_markdown: Calculate the probability that the delivery arrives between 15 and 25 minutes: $P(15 < X < 25) = \text{width} \times \text{height} = (25 - 15) \times \frac{1}{30}$. Enter as a fraction, decimal, or percentage.
stages.explanation_markdown: Because the uniform density is a rectangle of height $1/30$, the probability is simply the rectangular area: $P(15 < X < 25) = (25 - 15) \times \frac{1}{30} = \frac{10}{30} = \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.3333$ (or $33.33\%$).

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the expected (mean) delivery time $E[X]$ for this courier service?

options.hint_markdown: The width $b-a = 30$ represents the total spread, not the central balance point $(a+b)/2$.
Half the width is 15 minutes, but you must add the lower bound $a = 10$, giving $(10 + 40)/2 = 25$.

stages.explanation_markdown: The mean of a continuous uniform distribution is the midpoint of the support: $\mu = E[X] = \frac{a + b}{2} = \frac{10 + 40}{2} = 25.0$ minutes. Variance is $\sigma^2 = \frac{(b - a)^2}{12} = \frac{30^2}{12} = 75.0$, giving standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{75} \approx 8.66$ minutes.
